title: CHIA AI Tutor experiment v0.1
description: Project-owned experiment and result contract. Structural validity does not establish runtime or simulator support. All input bounds are provisional project limits, not hardware capability claims.

schema_version.description: Contract version; v0.1 is serialized as the quoted string 0.1.0.

metadata.description: Experiment identity and evidence references; not optimization knobs.

experiment_id.description: Unique run identifier. Give each candidate and each repetition its own ID.

description.description: Human-readable purpose or hypothesis for this experiment.

artifact_manifest.description: Path relative to this config, or URI, of run provenance and evidence. Null while unavailable. Must identify resolved software and hardware settings, revisions, measurement sources, and reasons for missing metrics. Reference existence/content is checked by the runner, not JSON Schema.

workload.description: Fixed comparison conditions. Hold these constant within a sweep; referenced protocols pin all controls omitted from this small schema.

dataset_id.description: Versioned evaluation question-set identifier; protocol pins split, item IDs, order, and reference answers.

corpus_id.description: Versioned retrieval corpus/index identifier; protocol pins chunks, embedding model, and index settings.

evaluation_protocol.description: Versioned protocol ID or path relative to this config. Defines scoring rubric, arrival schedule, warmup, decoding, context policy, timing boundaries, hardware baseline, and measurement methods.

num_questions.description: Number of evaluation questions per run, excluding warmup; unit: questions. Project budget bound.

seed.description: Seed supplied to supported sampling/runtime components; unit: dimensionless integer. Does not guarantee deterministic execution.

software.description: INPUT knobs owned by the software runner. Start with one fixed base model and vary the three primary numeric/precision knobs.

model.description: Base model registry identifier or local artifact path. Record immutable model/tokenizer revisions and actual quantized artifact in the run manifest. No model download or support check is performed by validation.

quantization.description: Primary knob: requested dominant weight format (16, 16, 8, or 4 bits respectively). fp16/bf16 are floating-point precision choices. This is not a complete quantization recipe and does not prescribe activation or arithmetic precision; manifest pins method, scales, grouping, kernels, and runtime.

retrieval_top_k.description: Primary knob: requested number of retrieved chunks per question; unit: chunks. v0.1 assumes retrieval enabled. Adapter must check corpus availability and context fit without silently changing k.

max_new_tokens.description: Primary knob: maximum generated tokens per answer, excluding input tokens; unit: tokens. Generation may stop earlier. Adapter checks model context limits.

batch_size.description: SECONDARY knob: maximum questions processed together in a static batch; unit: questions/batch. If omitted, runner uses 1. Default is an annotation, not inserted by this validator. Keep 1 in initial sweeps; final batch may be smaller. No dynamic batching policy is defined.

hardware.description: Provisional INPUT knobs for the modeled target CPU, not CHIA/Ray worker resources. Mapping and legal combinations must be verified against the exact gem5/BOOM implementation before execution.

l1_cache_kb.description: Requested L1 DATA cache capacity per target core; unit: KiB (1024 bytes), despite legacy _kb suffix. Instruction cache remains fixed by protocol. This interpretation is a v0.1 assumption requiring adapter verification.

l2_cache_kb.description: Requested total shared L2 capacity across target cores; unit: KiB (1024 bytes), despite _kb suffix. Shared topology is a provisional assumption; a private/banked topology must not be silently substituted.

cores.description: Target CPU core count; unit: cores. Does not set Ray worker count or software thread count. Protocol defines software threading policy.

issue_width.description: Requested maximum aggregate micro-operations issued toward execution per target core per cycle; unit: micro-operations/core/cycle. Provisional abstraction, not observed IPC. Exact mapping may involve multiple issue queues/ports; reject configurations without a verified equivalent mapping.

metrics.description: OUTPUT summaries produced by evaluators. All five keys are required; null means unavailable, never zero. Numeric values require evidence with measurement source and scope in the manifest.

answer_quality.description: Mean per-question rubric score normalized to [0,1]; unit: dimensionless fraction, not percent. Higher is better. Protocol pins rubric/evaluator; a score of 0.83 does not inherently mean 83% accuracy.

latency_ms.description: Mean time from each question's arrival to its complete answer, including queue/batch wait, retrieval, and generation; unit: milliseconds/question. Lower is better. Excludes model/index startup and protocol-defined warmup. Simulated target time must not be confused with host simulation wall time.

energy_joules.description: Total target-system energy over the evaluation interval divided by completed questions; unit: joules/question. Lower is better. Manifest states physical measurement or named calibrated estimate, component coverage, and idle-energy policy. Null until a defensible energy method exists.

memory_mb.description: Peak total resident memory attributable to the target tutor workload during evaluation; unit: decimal MB (1000000 bytes). Includes model, retrieval, activations, KV cache, and runtime under the protocol's accounting policy. Lower is better. Not model-file size or host simulator memory.

throughput_qps.description: Completed questions divided by seconds from first measured arrival to last measured completion; unit: questions/second. Higher is better. Uses the same evaluation interval as energy, excludes warmup, and includes batch/queue wait. Not tokens/second or generally the reciprocal of mean latency.

status.description: OUTPUT lifecycle state owned by orchestration, initialized as planned. A completed run is not proof of answer correctness or simulator validity.

state.description: planned: not started; running: in progress; completed: pipeline finished with at least one metric and evidence; failed: execution/evaluation could not finish. Partial metrics may remain on failed runs.

message.description: Human-readable context; required non-null on failure. Explain unavailable completed-run metrics here and in the manifest.
